rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: When the OPTION-A simplification removed the aggressive-mode block (section 6b) from bot_health_score() in /app/backend/routes/bot_routes.py, the `tilt_cfgs = await db.bot_configs.find(...).to_list(...)` line that was inside section 6b was removed with it — but section 7 (anti-tilt freeze, lines 1192-1240) still calls `for tc in tilt_cfgs`. Python evaluates that loop line as soon as the request runs, raising NameError. Every /api/bot/health-score call now returns 500, and the Bot Health page shows a red error banner. REPRODUCTION: `curl -c c.txt -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@trading.bot","password":"admin123"}'` then `curl -b c.txt $URL/api/bot/health-score` → 500 + 'Internal Server Error'. Backend log shows `File "/app/backend/routes/bot_routes.py", line 1198, in bot_health_score / for tc in tilt_cfgs: / NameError: name 'tilt_cfgs' is not defined`. MITIGATION (1-line): Just before line ~1197 add `tilt_cfgs = await db.bot_configs.find({'user_id': user['id']}).to_list(length=200)` OR fold section 7 into an existing bot_configs cursor. Optionally also wrap the whole handler in a try/except that returns a graceful degraded payload so the UI never shows a raw 500.
